holidays.name: World Turtle Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of turtles and tortoises, from tiny pond dwellers to ancient giants. People mark it by cleaning up beaches, protecting nesting sites, and generally showing some love to our shelled friends. Slow and steady wins the awareness race!
holidays.origin: World Turtle Day was created in 2000 by American Tortoise Rescue, a nonprofit group, to encourage people to learn about and protect turtles and tortoises and their disappearing habitats.
holidays.funFact: Turtles have existed for over 200 million years, which means they were around before dinosaurs had really gotten going, and they're still going strong.

holidays.name: National Lucky Penny Day
holidays.description: A day for spotting that shiny copper coin on the sidewalk, bending down to pick it up, and feeling smugly fortunate. Today you're allowed to believe in tiny, one-cent miracles.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin, inspired by the old superstition that finding a penny brings good luck.
holidays.funFact: The rhyme says that finding a penny and picking it up will bring you good luck all day long, and the superstition is often traced to the old belief that metal could ward off evil.

holidays.name: National Taffy Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the stretchy, chewy, jaw-testing candy that has been delighting (and gluing together) fillings for generations. Grab a piece of saltwater taffy and chew your way into the weekend of sweet nostalgia.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin, celebrating the classic pulled-sugar confection.
holidays.funFact: Saltwater taffy is famously associated with the Jersey Shore, yet it contains no actual seawater, and the name is said to have come from a boardwalk candy shop flooded during a storm.
